proposed_widenings.name: auto_hit
proposed_widenings.justification: Magic Missile's darts automatically hit with no attack roll and no saving throw. ActivationPhase is a union of attack_roll | save_gate only. There is no variant for unconditional/guaranteed damage delivery. Adding auto_hit (or direct_damage) as a third ActivationPhase variant would cover this spell and any other auto-hit effects.
proposed_widenings.evidence: A dart deals 1d4 + 1 Force damage to its target. The darts all strike simultaneously

proposed_widenings.name: dart_count_scaling
proposed_widenings.justification: Magic Missile scales on dart count (3 + 1 per slot level above 1), not on damage per dart or on a target-selection count. The existing choose_up_to TargetSelection with SlotScaling captures 'up to N different targets' semantics, but Magic Missile allows N darts to all hit the same creature. A dart_count parameter on the auto_hit phase (distinct from target selection) would model this correctly. Alternatively, the choose_up_to model could be reused if its semantics are loosened to 'N applications, may repeat target'.
proposed_widenings.evidence: The spell creates one more dart for each spell slot level above 1. The darts all strike simultaneously, and you can direct them to hit one creature or several.

notes: The spell cleanly fits the activation family (instantaneous, action cast time, no ongoing state). The sole blocker is the ActivationPhase union: attack_roll and save_gate are the only two variants, and neither applies — Magic Missile has no resolution step. A new auto_hit ActivationPhase variant is the narrowest fix. All v4 atoms needed (damage, target, scale_die_count) already exist; only the phase-level surface shape is missing. The dart-count scaling is a secondary design question: if choose_up_to is reinterpreted as 'N applications' it may suffice, but semantically it differs from 'up to N distinct creatures'.
